tools.name: lookup_firms_code
tools.description: Get the CBP FIRMS record for one code: facility name, status (active or deleted), facility type, address, CBP port, location, and the other codes registered at the same address. Deleted codes and "DO NOT USE" placeholders (junk: true) are returned with warnings. A code that is not on the list return

tools.name: search_firms_facilities
tools.description: Find FIRMS codes from a facility name and/or street address, e.g. 'maher terminal elizabeth' or '231 tyler st newark'. Typo-tolerant; returns ranked matches with a 0-100 score. Active codes only unless include_deleted is true. One call per search, however many results. Wraps GET /v1/search. Live key

tools.name: find_nearby_firms_facilities
tools.description: List FIRMS facilities within radius_km, nearest first. Pass exactly one origin: lat and lon; code (another FIRMS facility, left out of the results); or address (a US street address, geocoded unless it is a FIRMS facility's own address). meta.origin says which point was used. Facilities whose address

tools.name: validate_firms_code
tools.description: Pre-filing checks of a FIRMS code against the published CBP list, in order: format, exists (catches ACE reject 158), active (159), in the stated port (164), facility type fits the use (warehouse_entry: bonded warehouse 04; ftz_admission: FTZ 02; exam_site: CES 09; location_of_goods: not 07 or 08), n

tools.name: list_cbp_ports
tools.description: Every CBP port that has FIRMS codes, with name, state, region, facility_count and active_count, in one call. Wraps GET /v1/ports. Live keys (fapi_live_...): one counted call. Test keys (fapi_test_...): fixture sample data, not counted.

tools.name: get_cbp_port
tools.description: One CBP port with a page of its FIRMS facilities, ordered by code. Placeholders are left out; active codes only unless include_deleted is true. For the next page pass cursor = meta.next_cursor (null on the last page); each page is one call. Wraps GET /v1/ports/{port}. Live keys (fapi_live_...): one

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "lookup_firms_code" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_firms_code · Private data: lookup_firms_code · Public sink: validate_firms_code · Destructive: validate_firms_code.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_firms_code · Private data: lookup_firms_code · Public sink: validate_firms_code · Destructive: validate_firms_code

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
